about.title: Lancaster Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product rarely gives warning. In Lancaster, it might be a space heater that ignites on a cold night, a ladder that folds mid-climb, or a tire that separates at speed on Sierra Highway. Los Angeles County records show 1,051 injury collisions in Lancaster during 2025, with 1,723 people hurt, and some crashes trace back to a part that failed rather than a driver who erred. California treats these cases differently from ordinary negligence claims. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect, whether in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the store on Avenue K or Avenue J that sold it. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Lancaster residents with an independent attorney who takes these claims on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My tire blew out on Avenue K and I crashed. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. If the tire had a manufacturing or design defect, a product liability claim may exist alongside any auto claim, and strict liability means you would not have to show the tire maker was careless. The key is to keep the tire and the vehicle as they are so an expert can inspect them. An attorney in our network can sort out which claims apply.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability rule asks whether the product was defective in design, manufacture, or warnings, and whether that defect caused your injury. What the company knew or intended is usually not the deciding question. That said, each case turns on its facts, and an independent attorney can evaluate yours.

items.question: I already threw away the box and the receipt. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Losing the packaging does not automatically end a claim, though it can make things harder. If you still have the product, stop using it and store it somewhere safe. Bank statements, photos, and order histories can often stand in for a paper receipt. Reach out to LawProactive and we will connect you with an attorney who can assess what evidence remains.
